comparisons.peer_summary: The metrics include U.S. and non-U.S. commercial real estate loans with specific values provided for the years 2024, 2023, and 2022.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Bank of America report total commercial real estate (CRE) exposure metrics for 2024, though BAC breaks down its portfolio into U.S. and non-U.S. segments while Citi separates corporate and Wealth clients. Citi reported total CRE credit exposure of $65 billion, including $6 billion in office buildings (c_2024_7_P281_S001). Bank of America reported U.S. commercial real estate loans of $63.8 billion and non-U.S. commercial real estate loans of $6.1 billion for 2024, totaling approximately $69.9 billion (bac_2024_7_P058_S001).

sentences.text: As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, Citi's total credit exposure to commercial real estate (CRE) was $65 billion and $66 billion, including $6 billion and $8 billion of exposure related to office buildings, respectively.

comparisons.peer_summary: Credit exposure to OTC derivative counterparties that defaulted during 2024 remained low, representing less than 2% of total credit exposure from OTC derivatives.

sentences.text: As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, Citi's total credit exposure to commercial real estate (CRE) was $65 billion and $66 billion, including $6 billion and $8 billion of exposure related to office buildings, respectively.

Our credit exposure (before any potential recoveries) to OTC derivative counterparties that defaulted during 2024 remained low, representing less than 2% of our total credit exposure from OTC derivatives.
